steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Texas.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Salvadore Texas. What am I to think of you? Should I trust you?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: You are a Siracusan. They all say that violence and ambition runs in your veins. That you and your famiglia will devour this place... No, all of Columbia.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Is the man I see before my eyes truly you? So refined, so upstanding?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: But I've also seen the way you throw a punch, the blood dripping between your fingers until your opponent is not able to utter even a single curse.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Which is the real you, Salvadore?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Might there come a day when you realize that your two sides are as oil and water? Might there come a day when the trail of blood in your wake catches up to you?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: And when that day comes, what would you choose?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: When that day comes... would you remain by my side?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: A brilliant performance, signorina.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Without a doubt, you've surpassed my expectations yet again.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Actually, it's all thanks to someone in the troupe called Mr. Ben. I would never have been able to adjust so quickly without his advice.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Ben?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I'm not sure we have anyone by that name at Teatro di Milano.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: He was really knowledgeable about theater and gave me some extremely helpful pointers, so I figured he was an important person here.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Sorry, no one comes to mind. That said, there are plenty of enthusiasts around town who are very well-versed in plays. Perhaps he was one of them.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: More importantly, I saw something on your resume that had me a bit curious. Would you mind clarifying something for me?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Sure, ask away.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You've been pursuing a pop idol career in Lungmen.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: We've been collaborating with that city more and more recently, but our acting industries have often been at odds with each other, due to their different backgrounds.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But even with that caveat in mind, the clips from your audition sent over by Monster Siren Records convinced me that you have some musical talent.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: What this tells me, though, is that you have your sights set on a lot more than just Lungmen.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: What drives you to work so hard?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Well... a lot of different reasons, I'd say.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: But at the start, I didn't have anything complicated in mind. There was just someone I hoped to catch up to.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Hehe, it's just like in the script.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Every time she gazed through the window, or out the door, or across the empty streets, her eyes...

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Her eyes made me feel like, one day, she would leave both us and Lungmen behind.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: 'And when that day comes, what would you choose?'

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What's the hurry? Don't you think it's a miracle for the two of us to run into each other in Siracusa again?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'm busy right now.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What a coincidence, so am I.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Let me guess, your job is to protect this man?

steps.name: Bellone Bodyguard
steps.text: What are you—

steps.name: Bellone Bodyguard
steps.text: Eep...!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Some people really need to learn to read the room. Don't you agree, Texas?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Go protect the target. I'll deal with her.

steps.name: Bellone Bodyguard
steps.text: U-Understood!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So, want some mille-feuille?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: ...I'll take a piece.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Haha, now that's more like it!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: So, Texas. Whoops, now that we're in Siracusa, I should be calling you Cellinia, right?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'd rather you didn't.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Fine by me. Honestly, I find it easier that way, too. Force of habit can sure be a scary thing, can't it?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Living a leisurely life in Lungmen, occasionally bumping into each other at Rhodes Island, maybe even going on some missions together...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Makes me feel like my swords are gonna go rusty.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: This ever-familiar rain is what makes me feel alive.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Swords rust in the rain.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: In Siracusa, the rain washes away the blood.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Only people like you - who walk around town with your swords out but no intention to use them - need to worry about rust.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Why are you here?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It's simple, really. Because you are.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Hey, Texas, how long has it been since you were last in Siracusa?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Probably about ten years now?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Seven years and five months.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: For more than seven years, the prodigal daughter of Famiglia Texas has not set foot in Siracusa.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: I still remember how your grandfather sent you back here to serve as a hostage. You stayed with Famiglia Saluzzo for a while...

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Those days didn't last long, but we sure got along great, didn't we?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: If that's your idea of 'getting along.'

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Even though you're a Columbian, you managed to win the acknowledgment of all of Siracusa's famiglie.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Though, it was truly a shame what happened at the end.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: If you ask me, you ought to stay a while this time, and take a good look around.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'm going back as soon as I finish my work here.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh. Going back, you say?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Now that you mention it, there's something I've always been curious about, Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You betrayed the Texases and decided to become a lone wolf.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You even abandoned everything the Texases left behind in Columbia. So why do you still go by the name Texas in Lungmen?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: That's none of your business.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Lappland.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I don't plan on staying in Siracusa.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I will go back to Lungmen. There are people waiting for me there.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Okay then. I'll help you.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I don't need your help.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Surely you don't think this is a fight you can take all on your own?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Didn't you find some buddies over in Lungmen? Didn't your time at Rhodes Island teach you that it's okay to rely on others?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Siracusa is no place for tourists.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: If Rhodes Island ever plans to set up a branch office here, I would urge them to reconsider.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: But most of all, I can't trust you, specifically.

spans.text: But most of all, I can't trust

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Ah yes, trust.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Texas, you know my family name, right?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Saluzzo.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: That's right. And we Saluzzos don't place our bets lightly.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: You don't need to trust me, but you do need our backing, isn't that right?

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Or do you really intend to let the Bellones drag you around by the leash?
With a deafening boom, the sound of an explosion suddenly tore through the air from not too far away. The flash and flame effortlessly engulfed the government official by the name of Carracci.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: A car bomb?!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Oh? Now that's a classic.

steps.name: Bellone Bodyguard
steps.text: S-Signor Ministro!

steps.name: Bellone Bodyguard
steps.text: The banquet venue is under attack! All nearby famiglia associates, hurry and back us up!

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Damnit!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Simultaneous attacks on two fronts? Now that's interesting!

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: Who would have the guts to pull that off, Texas?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Show yourself.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: ...I knew it.
What should I do if I want to go back to Lungmen?
Ever since Texas took her first step back in this city, that question has always been on her mind.
Going by her agreement with Zaaro, the easiest way would be to obey Famiglia Bellone's every command.
But right now, Texas can already vaguely feel that—
The events unfolding in this city are not so simple.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Talk. Who sent you?

steps.name: Assassin
steps.text: You don't need to know.
But she is not worried.
She understands Siracusa well, and knows that there is no end to these things.
She simply feels a twinge of emptiness, one that even she never expected to feel. Because—
No one will come to her aid in this fight.
And after it's over, no one will ask her if she's hurt, or drag her off to some party.
For her, this emptiness has long since been second nature.
So much so that even after leaving Lungmen for such a brief period of time, everything about that city already seems so distant and nostalgic.

a.text: Don't stop me from going back home.'

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: But Texas.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: The more you want to go back, the more you'll have to cut your ties.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: It'll just make you sink deeper and deeper.

steps.name: Lappland
steps.text: What I want to know is, when you finally realize that you're completely covered in mud, what will you do then?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Good to see you again, Your Honor.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Oh, Danbrown, you're here. Looks like I'm in luck.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: You washed your car just last week, didn't you?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Nothing I can do about it. After all, it's my job to be hated.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Don't worry, I'll get it nice and clean again for you.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Why don't you take a look around while you wait?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That's alright, I'll just wait here.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Your Honor, I heard that judges have it pretty good.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: They drive fancy cars, show up on TV, and even the mayor has to be extra-polite around them.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: After all, they represent Signora Sicilia's will.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: I reckon I don't see any other judges like you, Signorina Lavinia, who get paint thrown on their car every other day.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You're probably right.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I don't know about the fancy cars or TV appearances, but I could sure use a membership card to your store right about now.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Sorry, our humble little shop doesn't offer VIP services.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You look like you're in a better mood than before though. Did that one famiglia stop giving you trouble?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: All thanks to you, Your Honor.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: I ran into them on the street yesterday, and they all steered clear of me.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Never thought there could be a judge as fair as you in Siracusa.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Fair, huh... They're just scared of the people behind me, that's all.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: You say that, but even if you're backed by Famiglia Bellone, you still doled out punishment to a famiglia well-connected with the Bellones.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: In Siracusa, Signora Sicilia is justice itself. I don't know how many of the judges representing the interests of her old famiglie actually bother upholding any real justice.

spans.text: In Siracusa, Signora Sicilia is justice itself. I don't know how many of the judges representing the interests of her old famiglie actually bother upholding any

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: But deep down in my heart, I know you're the embodiment of justice.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That isn't actually a compliment.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Oh right, I almost forgot. You said earlier that you were having trouble sleeping. Did you go see a doctor?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: I did. The doc said I didn't have anything wrong with me physically.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Just some mental stress.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Oh, is something troubling you?

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Troubling me...? I wouldn't go that far.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: Honestly, this job is basically just a way for me to kill time.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: I'm not exactly rich, but I'm not desperate for cash either.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: I don't know what I'm supposed to be doing, Your Honor. I just don't know.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: How do you usually like to pass the time?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: It's me.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: What?! Carracci was...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I understand. I'll be right there.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Sorry, Danbrown. Let's chat some other time.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: As for your question just now—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'd recommend giving the theater a shot. I often head down to watch an opera if I have the time to spare.
Danbrown exits the store.
He watches as the judge he deeply respects drive off into the rain, quickly disappearing from sight.
'She's always so busy,' he thinks to himself, drying his rain-beaded gloves on his overalls.
But nothing she does will end up mattering, will it?
Or rather, the fact that she still holds onto hope is precisely the reason why she'll be disappointed again and again.
Things weren't this complicated in the good old days. He looks at the rain falling outside the store, and suddenly remembers an afternoon many years ago.

steps.name: Carwash Worker
steps.text: I hope it rains a little longer, so I won't have to sweep out the garbage in the morning.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Get down!

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Eek—!

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Damn... Thought you were a pampered little princeling, but turns out you're pretty tough to deal with.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Tch, they're no slouches. Stand back, Rubio!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'm clearly the one they're after!

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: I, I know!

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Eek!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Tch, there's more of 'em over there too!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Out of my way!

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Slippery bastard.

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: What?! Isn't that Penguin Logistics'—

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Get down.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Ah, okay!

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: You dead, Gambino?

steps.name: Gambino
steps.text: Like I'd kick the bucket so easily. Tch, never expected the real master to show up here.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: Cut the crap.

steps.name: Capone
steps.text: The mission's botched. Let's split while we still can.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I think I remember those two...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: *cough* *cough*, *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Is everyone... gone now?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You alright?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I... think so...

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You're wounded. Don't move, it's easy to bleed out.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I've already called for backup. They'll be here soon.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'll be fine, but how...

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: How many people would've known about today's banquet?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Are you suggesting...?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You're right. Such a large-scale, coordinated attack must've been planned for a while.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But my identity is public knowledge at this point, and it's not exactly hard to track me down.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: In any case, I'm glad you arrived in time.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Carracci is dead.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: What did you say?!

steps.name: Wallach
steps.text: What?! You've gotta be shitting me...

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Carracci is... dead?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: A car bomb detonated right as he was walking by.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Carracci and three bodyguards near him died instantly.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Based on the wreckage at the scene, there was no point even taking him to the hospital.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The people who attacked us were without a doubt the same people who murdered Ministro Carracci. What could their objective be...?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Why are you here? There are so many court cars here as well—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You should've told me sooner that Bellone invited her here.

spans.text: You should've told me sooner that Bellone invited

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Cellinia Texas, as the first witness to the scene of Ministro Carracci's murder, you are also a suspect.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Now, I'm here to detain you.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Any resistance will be treated as flouting the laws of Siracusa, and will be punished accordingly.
Texas does not resist. She understands what she sees in the judge's eyes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Moreover...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: To all officials and associates of the famiglie, Ministro Carracci's importance to Volsinii is self-evident.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The attacks carried out on each of you will be investigated as part of the same investigation.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I, Lavinia Falcone, swear upon my honor to find the identity of the murderer. This shall not go unpunished!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You're not serious, are you?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Of course I am.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...Alright.
The string of events that just occurred makes Leontuzzo feel a bit fatigued.
And right as this thought crosses his mind, his entire world starts to spin.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leon!
The rain continues to fall, with no signs of relenting.
